correctness.rationale: Exact support function reduces intrinsic Haar width of Δ(n,k) to the Gaussian top-k minus bottom-k order-statistic sum divided by the centered Gaussian norm. At fixed α∈(0,1/2], trimmed-sum linearization gives the influence function (|G|−t)_+−E[(|G|−t)_+]−φ(t)(G²−1), whose Gaussian second moment equals the stated V(t). CLT yields width fluctuations, and width Lipschitz constant ≤√n with n−2-dimensional spherical concentration supplies uniform integrability and Var W→V(t). Continuity plus exact rational Gaussian bounds at t=1/2,1,5/4,3/2,2 forces a strict local minimum and maximum in the stated disjoint intervals; no uniqueness claim. Independently evaluated V at those five rational thresholds, reproducing 0.01488462, 0.00581403, 0.00787487, 0.00870885, 0.00541904, all correct strict inequalities. The all-n CLT is analytical; numeric checks do not prove it.
residual_risks: Fixed positive α only, not sparse vanishing-rank regimes. Strict two extrema existence, not exact number. Gaussian variance convergence requires concentration argument, not proved by finite samples.
